SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which sentence helps you remember the cardinal points in clockwise order? (1 mark)
   A. Eat Slowly Now Wisely
   B. Never Eat Slimy Worms
   C. Some Old Men Walk
   D. Watch Every Sunny Night

2. What should you find first when you read a map? (1 mark)
   A. The north arrow
   B. The colours
   C. The size of the paper
   D. The names of rivers

3. What is a neighbouring county? (1 mark)
   A. The biggest county
   B. A county in another country
   C. A county with the same name
   D. A county that shares a boundary with your county

4. Which county has a neighbouring county called Kiambu to its north? (1 mark)
   A. Mombasa
   B. Kisumu
   C. Turkana
   D. Nairobi

5. A pupil says that a county with many people must be the biggest in area. What is wrong with this idea? (1 mark)
   A. Area and population are different things
   B. People make land bigger
   C. Counties never have people
   D. Only farms make counties big

6. What is a mountain? (1 mark)
   A. A wide flat area
   B. A large body of water
   C. Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   D. A low place between hills

7. Why are mountains important for water? (1 mark)
   A. They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   B. They dry up lakes
   C. They make the land flat
   D. They stop all rain

8. What is a physical feature? (1 mark)
   A. A building made by people
   B. A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   C. A market
   D. A road

9. Why do farmers plan their work using seasons? (1 mark)
   A. Seasons decide school holidays only
   B. Seasons tell the price of clothes
   C. Seasons decide the colour of soil
   D. Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested

10. Which season usually follows the long rains in Kenya's common pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Short rains
   B. Cool or cold season
   C. Long rains again
   D. Hot season

11. Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles? (1 mark)
   A. Sunburn
   B. Broken leg
   C. Toothache
   D. Malaria

12. Which is the best source of information about a historic place near you? (1 mark)
   A. A guess
   B. A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   C. A rumour
   D. An advert for soap

13. What is a cultural centre? (1 mark)
   A. A place for repairing cars
   B. A hospital
   C. A bank
   D. A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive

14. What should you do when visiting a museum? (1 mark)
   A. Shout loudly
   B. Take objects home
   C. Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   D. Run around the halls

15. Which of these is a good? (1 mark)
   A. Driving a matatu
   B. Nursing
   C. A pair of shoes
   D. Teaching

16. What is barter? (1 mark)
   A. Exchanging one thing for another without money
   B. Buying with money only
   C. Stealing
   D. Giving things away

17. In a chart of who gives and who needs, what does a nurse give? (1 mark)
   A. Transport
   B. Food
   C. Learning
   D. Health care

18. In a bar graph of sub-county populations, which sub-county has the tallest bar? (1 mark)
   A. The one with the fewest people
   B. The largest area
   C. The one with the most people
   D. The smallest area

19. Why is population distribution useful to county planners? (1 mark)
   A. It helps them to move rivers
   B. It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   C. It helps them to change the weather
   D. It helps them to grow tea

20. On a dot map where one dot means 1,000 people, an area has 7 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 7,000
   B. 70
   C. 70,000
   D. 700

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how health workers, farmers and teachers depend on each other. (4 marks)

22. State two things a good map key should show. (2 marks)

23. Explain two ways of showing appreciation to people who help us. (2 marks)

24. Explain why we say that the compass is useful in a county. (5 marks)

25. Give three reasons why people need directions in everyday life. (3 marks)

26. Explain what may happen if people cut down all the trees on a mountain. (3 marks)

27. On a sketch map the school is in the middle, the market is above it and the clinic is below it. Write two sentences to say where the market and the clinic are. (4 marks)

28. Explain why many families live near towns and rivers. (3 marks)

29. State two things that a visitor can learn in a museum. (2 marks)

30. Why should you never shelter under a tall tree during a thunderstorm? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — TERMLY EXAM #13 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Never Eat Slimy Worms
   The first letters N, E, S, W give north, east, south, west in clockwise order.

2. A — The north arrow
   Finding north first helps you read all other directions.

3. D — A county that shares a boundary with your county
   Neighbouring counties touch each other along a boundary.

4. D — Nairobi
   Kiambu lies to the north of Nairobi County.

5. A — Area and population are different things
   Size is about area. Population is the number of people.

6. C — Very high land with steep sides and a peak
   A mountain is much higher than the land around it.

7. A — They catch rain and give rise to rivers
   Mountains catch rain and feed rivers.

8. B — A natural feature on the surface of the Earth
   Physical features such as mountains and rivers are natural.

9. D — Crops need the right weather to grow and be harvested
   Planting and harvesting depend on rain and dry weather.

10. B — Cool or cold season
   In the usual pattern, June to August is cool or cold in many places.

11. D — Malaria
   Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

12. B — A resource person such as an elder or a guide
   Elders and guides know the true story of the place.

13. D — A place where the culture of communities is shown and kept alive
   Cultural centres show dances, homes, crafts and foods.

14. C — Listen to the guide and do not touch objects unless allowed
   Good manners protect the objects and other visitors.

15. C — A pair of shoes
   Goods are things we can touch and use.

16. A — Exchanging one thing for another without money
   Barter means swapping goods, such as a goat for grain.

17. D — Health care
   Nurses give health care.

18. C — The one with the most people
   Taller bars show bigger values.

19. B — It helps them to place schools, clinics and roads where people live
   Services should reach people where they live.

20. A — 7,000
   7 x 1,000 = 7,000.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Health workers keep farmers and teachers well. Farmers give food to health workers and teachers. Teachers teach the children of farmers and health workers. Each group needs the others to live well.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct link.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: The meaning of the colours and the meaning of the lines or symbols used on the map.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

23. (2 marks)
   Answer: Say thank you and treat their work with respect. Accept helping them in return.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: It helps us to find our way. It helps mapmakers to draw maps. It helps us to describe where places are. It helps drivers and sailors to travel. It helps us to plan journeys.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid point, up to 5.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: To find places, to travel safely, and to explain to others where something is. Accept sailors, pilots and farmers using direction.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible reason.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Rain may wash away the soil. Rivers may dry up. There may be landslides or floods.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct result.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: The market is north of the school. The clinic is south of the school.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct direction word and 1 mark for each correct sentence.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Towns have jobs, schools and shops. Rivers give water for drinking and farming. These things make life easier.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for towns, 1 mark for rivers, 1 mark for making life easier.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: How people lived long ago and which tools they used. Accept learning about animals, plants and cultures.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lightning can strike tall trees. It is safer to go into a strong building.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the danger, 1 mark for a safer choice.
